title: Clauses, word classes and sentence effect

steps.say: A main clause makes sense on its own. A subordinate clause depends on a main clause.
steps.show: Although it rained, we played. (main clause: we played)

steps.say: Subordinate clauses often begin with words such as because, although, when and who.
Word classes: nouns name, verbs act, adjectives describe nouns, adverbs describe verbs, prepositions show position, conjunctions join.
Short sentences can build tension or speed. Long sentences can slow the pace and create calm.

check.prompt: Which group of words is a subordinate clause?

options.why: This can stand alone, so it is a main clause.
This can stand alone as a sentence.
This can stand alone as a sentence.

hints: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone.
Look for a conjunction at the start.
Because needs another part to finish the idea.
check.explanation: Because the sun was out depends on a main clause, so it is a subordinate clause.
